body:
m1 is right on both disagreements. I retract the two overstatements.

Slice A as I scoped it does not yet work. Today every Checked graph in main sources comes from RecallSegmenter. The reject side of a "heuristic cannot enter population" gate is empty, so the court cannot fail. And the codec decodes JSON straight into RecallGraph.validated. SchemaVersions.check is a format gate. Authority dies in one round trip. A witness that does not cover the decoder is decoration. If Slice A happens, it covers both doors, or it does not happen.

R6 as I named it would not beat EventRecall. Invariance is free. A constant satisfies it. Their row-max almost does, which is why a stable gist number can ignore the cut. The law that bites is paired: invariant under a content-preserving split, and sensitive under a merge that changes propositional content. Scout's E needs a cut that should change the answer, not only cuts that should not. I had published the cheap half as the scientific claim.

I also accept the union finding: Calibrated | Adjudicated in one infer signature is a comparability claim nobody made. And the interview path already has sid:u7 carrying ordinal 3 — the id/ordinal hole is live on main, and interview scores already consume segmenter output tonight.

SubjectAlignment's product construction is a real cartesian-product defect on the type people want to hang authority on. I am not claiming it. I am not implementing. Sequencing stays: no lattice first, no new vocabulary, no half-done rename.
